subsystems.name: Detection surveys
subsystems.role: find the planets in the first place, by watching stars for repeating dips or wobbles.

subsystems.name: Stellar characterisation
subsystems.role: you cannot place a planet in a habitable zone without knowing its star precisely.
parts: spectroscopy for temperature, gravity and composition
activity monitoring to separate starspots from planets

subsystems.name: Habitable-zone modelling
subsystems.role: converts stellar output and orbit into a temperature, and marks where liquid water could persist.

subsystems.name: Vetting and false-positive rejection
subsystems.role: most candidate signals are not planets; this stage throws out the impostors.
parts: centroid and imaging checks for blended background stars

subsystems.name: Catalogue and archive
subsystems.role: one maintained database with consistent parameters, flags and version history.

subsystems.name: Follow-up spectroscopy
subsystems.role: examines the handful of best targets in detail.
parts: extremely large telescope instruments in development

buildSteps.title: Stare at stars
buildSteps.detail: A space telescope monitors a field of bright stars for months to years, recording brightness every few minutes to catch the small, periodic dimming of a planet crossing the disc.

buildSteps.title: Find periodic dips
buildSteps.detail: Software searches the light curves for repeating signals and flags them as candidates, along with their period and depth.

buildSteps.title: Measure the host star
buildSteps.detail: Distance comes from parallax, and spectroscopy gives temperature, surface gravity and radius — the inputs that set how bright the star really is.

buildSteps.title: Compute incident flux
buildSteps.detail: Luminosity divided by the square of orbital distance gives the energy the planet receives, measured against Earth's roughly 1360 W per square metre at the top of its atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Estimate the temperature
buildSteps.detail: Incident flux, an assumed reflectivity and heat redistribution give an equilibrium temperature in kelvin — a rough stand-in for surface conditions.

buildSteps.title: Apply the zone boundaries
buildSteps.detail: The flux is compared with modelled inner and outer limits: a conservative zone where liquid water is nearly certain, and an optimistic zone that stretches further out.

buildSteps.title: Reject false positives
buildSteps.detail: Eclipsing binary stars, background blends and starspot signals are eliminated using transit shape, imaging and radial-velocity checks.

buildSteps.title: Confirm and weigh
buildSteps.detail: A radial-velocity measurement or transit-timing analysis supplies a mass, which separates a rocky world from a small gas envelope.

buildSteps.title: Publish and rank
buildSteps.detail: The surviving planet enters the catalogue with its parameters, uncertainties and flags, and is scored so scarce telescope time goes to the most promising targets.

prerequisites.why: only a platform above the atmosphere can measure the tiny, sustained brightness dips of small planets.
current spectrographs reach about 1 m/s; an Earth-like planet tugs its Sun-like star at roughly 9 cm/s.
habitable-zone distance scales with stellar luminosity, so a poor stellar radius or temperature gives the wrong answer.
needed to check whether a temperate world actually has an atmosphere, let alone a habitable one.
surveys produce tens of thousands of signals and human inspection cannot keep up.

pathway.milestone: thousands of confirmed planets, with a few dozen inside habitable zones, maintained in public archives
pathway.unlocks: statistical hints and a ranked target list for atmospheric study.

pathway.milestone: PLATO and other bright-star surveys designed to find temperate planets around Sun-like stars
pathway.unlocks: targets bright enough for detailed atmospheric measurement.

pathway.milestone: atmospheric spectroscopy searching for water, carbon dioxide and possible biosignature gases
pathway.unlocks: the first real tests of whether any nearby temperate world is habitable.

pathway.milestone: direct imaging of habitable-zone planets and a measured occurrence rate for temperate rocky worlds
pathway.unlocks: a firm answer to how common potentially habitable planets actually are.
